clue.text: A doctor, stupid fellow, with a frock for the envoy's wife

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A dim doctor in a frock is mistaken for an ambassador's wife at a diplomatic party.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run A + MB + ASS + A DRESS; MB is the British medical degree often used for a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassadress is traditionally the title given to the spouse of an ambassador, who is an envoy.

clue.text: Painter upset by competitor's approach

indicators.note: in a down clue something upset is turned over, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword painter

explanation.surface: An artist is thrown off balance as a rival draws near.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is the act of coming near or reaching a place, which is what an approach means.

clue.text: Cooked up crazy ideas on old railway organisation

indicators.note: ideas that are crazy and stirred up are muddled, so the letters are jumbled
in a down clue on means placed beneath, so the preceding words come second

parts.note: British Rail, the former national railway
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dreamed up mad schemes for how the old railway should be run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked up' reads as one phrase meaning invented, but the definition is just 'Cooked'; in a down clue 'on' puts the second piece below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is to cook food slowly in a little liquid in a closed pot.

clue.text: Follower of Helios not so quick to embrace riotous fun

indicators.note: riotous suggests disorder, so the following letters are thrown into a new order
to embrace is to hold something inside one's arms, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A devotee of the Greek sun god is too sluggish to join in the wild fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Helios is the Greek sun god; the flower is famous for turning its head to follow the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunflowers turn their heads through the day to track the sun, so they follow Helios, its Greek personification.

clue.text: Judgement on conflict in modern times

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it

explanation.surface: A verdict is passed on a war of recent years.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a decision handed down by an arbitrator or judge, so it is a formal judgement.

clue.text: Ridiculous increase, getting one pound back

indicators.note: getting means receiving, so the first word takes the others into itself
back means the word for pound is read the wrong way round

parts.note: the abbreviation for a pound weight

explanation.surface: A pay rise of just one pound is laughable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risible provokes laughter, so it is laughable or absurd.

clue.text: Italian lady soldiers going up to girl

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom upward

explanation.surface: Troops advance towards a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Signora is the Italian title for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs or madam.

clue.text: Increasing value of sympathetic criticism

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rise in worth, as of property
second meaning: an understanding critical assessment of a work

explanation.surface: A critic's kind review boosts the worth of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a gain in the market worth of an asset and a perceptive, admiring critique of art.

clue.text: Relate to exercises in art, perhaps…

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Wondering whether exercises bear on art, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is part of the letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain to something is to concern it or be connected with it.

clue.text: … when getting point, for example, on first-class weapon

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a top-quality weapon gets a sharp point.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class, and in crosswords the 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Look closely into and harangue examining body

explanation.surface: Someone investigates and lectures a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspectorate is an official organisation of inspectors whose job is checking standards.

clue.text: Going over in opposition to one's real case

indicators.note: a case holds something, so the last word wraps around the others

parts.note: taken as written; it is split around the other pieces
one is I, and 's is read as is

explanation.surface: Reviewing evidence against someone's genuine legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: A revisal is a revision, the act of going over something again to correct it.

clue.text: They owe something to wild bet accepted by the late Diana

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by, so one piece sits inside another
wild means out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: Diana Dors, the British film actress who died in 1984

explanation.surface: A film star's reckless wager leaves people in her debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana Dors was a British film actress and sex symbol of the 1950s, already dead when this was set.
explanation.definitionFit: Debtors are people who owe money or something else to a creditor.

clue.text: Warm hat commonly associated with chartered accountant

parts.note: lid is everyday slang for a hat

explanation.surface: An accountant is known for wearing a cosy hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The accountant comes first in the answer though last in the clue; 'commonly' flags lid as colloquial.
explanation.definitionFit: Calid is a rare word, from Latin calidus, meaning hot or warm.

clue.text: Extensively a predicament in Wales, perhaps

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it
perhaps hints the place name could be arranged another way

parts.note: to be in a hole is to be in trouble
the letters of this name, rearranged

explanation.surface: There is widespread trouble across Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, wholesale means on a large scale or indiscriminately, so extensively.

clue.text: In general, one accepts a grave problem

indicators.note: a problem is something tangled, so the letters are worked into a new order
accepts means takes in, so one word holds the rest

parts.note: taken as written; it is split around the rest

explanation.surface: As a rule, a person takes on a serious difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: On average means usually or typically, considering things as a whole.

clue.text: Tree presenting problems for some of you

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a genus of conifers including the monkey puzzle

definitions.text: presenting problems for some of you
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the pen name of a famous Guardian crossword setter

explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria (John Graham) was the Guardian's best-loved setter, whose puzzles gave solvers plenty of problems; the monkey puzzle tree adds a hidden pun on puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the botanical genus of the monkey puzzle and the pseudonym of a setter who devised puzzles for readers.

clue.text: Rag once used to gather moss

indicators.note: something used is worn and knocked about, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An old cloth was once used to collect moss.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrogen is a flowerless plant growing from its tip, such as a fern or moss, so moss is an example.

clue.text: Baby with obsequious charm?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an infant not yet walking, who moves on all fours
second meaning: a toady who flatters to win favour

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second definition is loose: a person with obsequious charm, a sycophant.
explanation.definitionFit: A crawler is both an infant who crawls and, informally, a person who fawns on superiors.

clue.text: Weight of vehicle at rear

parts.note: the word at, placed at the back

explanation.surface: How heavy a car is at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat is a unit of weight for gemstones, equal to 200 milligrams.

clue.text: After tea, read about pantomime

indicators.note: about suggests turned around and moved, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: char or cha is British slang for tea
the letters of this word, rearranged

explanation.surface: After teatime, someone reads about a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime here means a mimed performance, not the British Christmas show.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is a game or act of mimed guessing, a piece of dumbshow, which is what pantomime can mean.

clue.text: Withdraw what was said about region

parts.note: a tract is an expanse of land

explanation.surface: Taking back one's remarks on a certain area.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to take it back or formally disown it.

clue.text: Fashionable ways to make encroachments

explanation.surface: Trendy methods of intruding on others' territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are advances into territory or intrusions on something, as in making inroads.

clue.text: Rustic one swallowed by bird

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside the swallower

explanation.surface: A country dweller is gulped down by a large bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is a country youth or rustic lover in pastoral poetry.

clue.text: He may be too strict in demanding payments from retired player

definitions.text: He may be too strict in demanding payments

explanation.surface: A former actor is now a harsh debt collector.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is one who exacts, insisting harshly on payment such as tribute or taxes.

clue.text: Boy the French see as a flower

explanation.surface: The French regard a lad as a blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella is a genus of garden plants, including love-in-a-mist, grown for its blooms.

clue.text: Very hard for first male worker

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: Labour was tough for the first man.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant originally named an impenetrably hard stone, so it describes something extremely hard.

clue.text: Gate soldiers go to first in a state of joy

parts.note: a gate is a way in

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the preceding word is used

explanation.surface: Troops pass through a gate first, in high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrancement is the condition of being entranced, filled with delight or rapture.
